topics.topic: Admissibility and validation order of schemas on bindings, flow ports, and constants
questions: Must unsupported schemas on flow ports or constants be refused at composition, and at what check position?
Must every schema appearing in a binding, flow port or constant belong to the supported JSON Schema subset, and at which operation is an unsupported schema refused?
Are unsupported schemas on binding ports refused at proposal and acceptance, and at what position in rule 5's order?

quotes:
Any other keyword —
   `$ref`, `pattern`, `format`, `oneOf`, `anyOf`, `allOf`, `not` among them —
   is outside the subset: A02 refuses it in a contract version, and
   `fit_port_value` answers that no value fits it, so a binding or flow port
   written outside the subset can never deliver.
judgement.why: State 6 specifies that contracts refuse unsupported schemas while binding and flow ports may contain them but can never deliver a fitting value.

topics.topic: Allowed service base-URL forms and exact path and authority joining rules
questions: Are credentials, query strings and fragments forbidden in `api_base_url`, and exactly how is a non-root base path joined to the operation path?

Are user information, query, fragment, an existing path, noncanonical ports or multiple trailing slashes permitted in `api_base_url`, and exactly how are they joined and represented in the `Host` header?
Which exact base-URL forms are allowed, and how are they joined without normalization or authority changes?

judgement.why: This is the same base-URL grammar and deterministic joining question previously assigned to a later state.

precedent.topic: Valid service base URLs and deterministic joining with operation paths
precedent.why: The accepted base-URL grammar, joining rules and Host serialization are format and encoding details belonging to State 6.

topics.topic: Canonical ordering and first-failure order for tied flow edges and constants
questions: What tie-breaker canonicalizes distinct edges or constants whose stated sort keys are equal?
If tied edges fail different guard checks, which edge is the first failure?

What tie-breaker canonicalizes two edges with identical endpoint tuples but different guards, or two constants with the same target but different values, before their invalid flow version is hashed and kept?
What tie-breakers order and hash edges whose listed edge-order keys are equal?
What tie-breaker determines the identity and deterministic first failure when constants have the same destination but different values or classes?

judgement.why: This is the same missing tie-breaker question for canonical edge and constant ordering.

precedent.topic: Canonical ordering of tied edges and constants for identity and proof checks
quotes:
Lists
   whose order carries no meaning are sorted before hashing — ports by
   (`direction`, `name`), nodes by `node_id`, edges in the edge order of A05,
   constants by (`to_node`, `to_port`) — so the same content in another order has
   the same identity; list values themselves keep their order.
precedent.why: The missing tie-breakers were already present in the unchanged identity-ordering rule.

topics.topic: Conversion and truncation of arbitrary response bytes into service failure detail
questions: How are non-UTF-8 or binary response bytes converted into failure-detail text before truncation?
How is an arbitrary non-UTF-8 response body converted into bounded textual `failure_detail`, and is the kept portion a prefix or another excerpt?
How is failure_detail produced from arbitrary response bytes, and which bytes are retained?

judgement.why: This is the same arbitrary response-byte conversion and failure-detail truncation question.

precedent.topic: Binary error-body conversion and failure-detail length measurement
quotes:
The body of
   an error response is not interpreted; at most `failure_detail_bytes_max` of it
   is kept as `failure_detail`, whose class is the highest of the execution's
   class and the classes the binding declares for its outputs, under A07 rule 5.
precedent.why: The error-body-to-text and length questions already arose from this unchanged passage and were not made material by the change.

topics.topic: Exact interpreter, runtime, dependency, and sandbox versions defining release v1
questions: Which CPython 3.12 patch release and build are part of release v1's exact runtime identity?
Which exact dependency and bubblewrap versions constitute release v1?
What exact dependency and runtime versions constitute release v1?

quotes:
A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list.
judgement.why: The runtime-version passage was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make the missing patch, build, dependency or bubblewrap versions matter.

topics.topic: Required completeness and exactness of authored trial input and expected-output maps
questions: Must trial inputs be exactly the input-port set, and when expected outputs are present must they be complete or may they be a subset?
When `expected_outputs` is present, must it contain exactly every contract output port, or may it assert only a subset?
Must an authored case supply every input exactly once and, when expected_outputs is present, every output exactly once; and are unknown or partial port maps refused?

judgement.why: This is the same trial-case input and expected-output completeness question.

precedent.topic: Required completeness of authored trial-case inputs and expected outputs

topics.topic: Total ordering of records created within one atomic store transaction
questions: What positions do records written by one store call receive relative to each other, and therefore how do paging, activation identities and oldest-first recovery observe them?
How are multiple newly created records in the same transaction ordered relative to one another, especially where paging, ‘oldest’ or activation identity observes store position?
How are records written by the same transaction ordered relative to one another, and which record kinds participate in the single order?

judgement.why: This is the same question about ordering records created in one transaction.

precedent.topic: Store ordering of records created within one atomic transaction
quotes:
The kernel is one process with one store and one writer. A change is one call in
one transaction inside the store module; callers do not open, name or pass
transactions.
precedent.why: The relative order of multiple records in one transaction was already unresolved and the change did not create that issue.

topics.topic: Valid and safely encoded multipart field names and disposition parameters
questions: Which port names are valid for multipart use, or how are disposition parameter values escaped and encoded?
How are quotes, backslashes, non-ASCII text and other characters in port names encoded or refused so they cannot alter multipart headers?
Which port names are legal in multipart bindings, and how are disposition parameters escaped or encoded?

judgement.why: This is the same multipart port-name validity and escaping question.

precedent.topic: Escaping and validity rules for port names in multipart headers
quotes:
Each part has exactly two
   headers: `Content-Disposition: form-data; name="<port>"`, with
   `filename="<port>"` added for a file part, and `Content-Type`, the port's
   media type for a file part and `application/json` for a value part, without
   parameters; nothing else.
precedent.why: Multipart port-name escaping was already unresolved by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Which release ceilings govern existing artifacts and resubmissions after an upgrade

Which non-contract artifacts are grandfathered under the release that created them, and which are rechecked against the currently running release's ceilings?

topics.topic: Atomicity, ordering, and durable failure semantics for oversized mapped aggregate outputs
questions: If a mapped node has several output ports and only one aggregated list exceeds the ceiling, are valid lists from its other outputs delivered, or does the aggregate node publish no outputs at all? In what output-port order are sizes checked?
How is the failure durable and explainable when the mapped output feeds only a flow output or has no dependent node that can record `upstream_failed`?

quotes:
No record states that
   failure itself, and none is needed: the dependants' `upstream_failed`
   records, written in the change that first derives it, are its durable
   fact, and until they exist nothing has observed it, so a derivation after
   a restart — under a release whose ceiling may differ — decides afresh with
   nothing to contradict;

The trace is the only source the kernel uses to explain or continue a run;
   process logs are never an input to a kernel decision.
judgement.why: A13 says an oversized mapped aggregate failure may have no record, while A15 requires the trace to be the sole source for explaining and continuing the run.

topics.topic: Canonical equality semantics for guard values
questions: Is guard equality canonical-JSON equality, JSON structural equality, host-language equality, or another comparison—especially for numbers, booleans, arrays and objects?

quotes: advance_run: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] The next node is the ready node with the smallest node_id; a node is ready when every input port holds its value: flow inputs delivered along every edge from them, constants to their port, and outputs of a concluded succeeded node along every edge whose guard is absent or whose guard port value equals the guard value as canonical JSON text.
judgement.why: The later notes define guard comparison as equality of canonical JSON text.

topics.topic: Durable identification of the exact FlowActivation authorizing a draft write

`SpooledFilesRef`
    gains `disclosure_class`, the class of the file list it names, so an empty

      operation node names a binding in status `accepted`;
judgement.why: The phase-1 treatment of missing node references was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make its interaction with the general unknown-reference rule matter.

topics.topic: Meaning and runtime validation of value_schema for file ports
questions: What does a file port's `value_schema` validate at trial and run time: file bytes, metadata, or nothing beyond schema equality between ports?
What does a file port's value_schema describe, and which schema checks, if any, are performed on file bytes at authoring, trial and run time?

quotes:
A `file` port's `value_schema` is the empty schema `{}`; its fit
   is its media type (State 5, `fit_port_value`).

fit_port_value: [SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT] A file's content is never opened or inspected: the schema check of a file port compares each candidate file's media_type with the port's media_type as exactly equal text, and the size check compares each file's size_bytes with size_bound per file, never their sum.
judgement.why: State 6 defines a file port's schema as the empty schema and runtime fitting as media-type and size checks without inspecting bytes.

topics.topic: Outcome classification after final HTTP headers but incomplete response body
questions: If final headers arrive but the body times out, resets or ends prematurely, has a valid final response been received, and is a non-read 4xx `not_applied` or `unknown`, and a 2xx `applied` or `unknown`?
For a non-read request whose final status is known but whose body is incomplete, is the attempt unknown, applied/not_applied according to status, or a contract violation?

quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.
judgement.why: The later invoker contract gives timeout, reset or end-of-stream precedence after any request byte was written, producing unknown for non-read effects.

topics.topic: Output-byte accounting and outcome precedence for noncanonical or invalid sandbox outputs
questions: How is `output_bytes` computed when the returned object is structurally invalid or contains a value with no canonical JSON form, and which outcome wins?
How is `output_bytes` evaluated when an output cannot be canonically encoded, and which outcome wins if that output is also very large?

judgement.why: This is the same output-accounting and classification question for values that cannot be canonically encoded.

precedent.topic: Classification and size-limit precedence for uncanonicalizable returned values
quotes:
The output count is the sum of the canonical JSON bytes of every
   `value` output and the bytes of every `file` output of the one call of `run` —
   for a `many` file output, the sum of its elements' bytes.
precedent.why: The counting of uncanonicalizable outputs was already unresolved by this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Required manifest field types, canonicalization, failure classification, and check order
questions: What exact manifest shape is required, and what happens when fields such as `capabilities`, capability entries, `required_headers`, or a read operation's `idempotency_key` have the wrong JSON type?
Which manifest shape and type errors are `manifest mismatch`, and where do they appear in rule 5's first-failure order?
What happens when a read operation's idempotency_key is a number, object, array or boolean?

judgement.why: This is the same manifest-schema and malformed-record precedence question assigned to State 6.

precedent.topic: Manifest schema validation and refusal precedence for malformed records
precedent.why: The exact manifest schema, nested field types and malformed-shape validation belong to State 6.

topics.topic: Resolution of a configured manifest revision to an atomic byte snapshot
questions: What concrete snapshot operation maps `manifest_location` plus `manifest_revision` to the bytes read by the kernel?
How is a file read at a repository revision, and does a missing, invalid or unavailable revision stop kernel startup or merely make later manifest reads fail?

quotes:
**The manifest at a revision**: `manifest_location` is a directory inside a
   git repository and `manifest_revision` a commit of it; `bindings` reads
   `<service_id>.json` of that directory at that commit as a git object, never
   from the working tree, so a record changes only with the configured revision
   (A08 rules 1 and 6).

**A manifest that cannot be read at start** in
   `bindings.check_installed_instances`: the start stops and names it; every
   start step is required (State 3, "Start").
judgement.why: The later text defines revision reads as Git-object reads at a commit and makes an unreadable startup manifest stop startup.

topics.topic: Scope of the sandbox prohibition on clocks and time observation
questions: Is the requirement merely to trap the enumerated APIs, or must the sandbox guarantee observational determinism and absence of every clock-like source?
Are unlisted clock-like standard-library entry points permitted because the release list is exhaustive, or must every way for function code to observe time be blocked?

judgement.why: This is the same question about whether the closed trap list exhausts the no-clock requirement.

precedent.topic: Whether every mechanism for observing clock time must be prohibited
quotes:
The list is closed for the release; an
   entry point found missing is added by a new release.
precedent.why: The completeness of the clock-trap list was already at issue in this unchanged passage.

topics.topic: Validity or required rerun of admission verdicts across runtime releases
questions: Does an admission verdict produced under an earlier runtime remain valid after an upgrade, or must the implementation be re-executed under the new release?
Does an admission verdict remain valid after a release changes execution behavior, or must admission be rerun or keyed by release?

judgement.why: This is the same question about reuse of admission verdicts across runtime releases.

precedent.topic: Validity of admissions and executions across kernel runtime releases
quotes:
Submitting an implementation — new, or equal to an existing one — runs
   admission unless an AdmissionVerdict M08 for that implementation and the
   current corpus digest already exists, in which case that verdict is used.

A release pins the exact versions of the kernel's Python dependencies and of
   the sandbox runtime (A03); the sandbox interpreter of release v1 is CPython
   3.12, whose `random` module gives A03 rule 4 its list. A vulnerable dependency is answered by a new
   release; a running kernel never updates one.

a function element without a
   concluded record is executed again, which is safe because it is pure;
precedent.why: Verdict reuse is keyed only by implementation and corpus, with no release exception, while restart re-executes unfinished functions using the runtime pinned by the installed release.

topics.topic: Whether empty flow node identifiers are allowed and distinguishable from endpoints
questions: May a node have the empty string as its identifier, and if so how is it distinguished and ordered against a flow endpoint?

quotes:
A flow input
   or flow output endpoint has the empty string as its node, so it orders before
   every node.
judgement.why: The empty-string endpoint convention was unchanged, and the reopening change did not make node-identifier emptiness matter.

topics.topic: Whether standing grants may name function nodes and when they are rejected
questions: Is a grant request naming a function node refused, and at what point in the grant checks?
Is a grant request naming a function node refused, or can it create an active grant that is never used?

quotes: grant_standing_approval: [VALIDATION_ERROR] MUST check in this order and raise on the first failure: the flow through active_flow_version, letting UnknownReferenceError propagate for a flow that does not exist; RefusedError when the flow has no active version; RefusedError when node_id is not a node of that active version, read with read_flow_version; RefusedError when the node's kind is function; RefusedError when the effect_class of the node's binding, read with read_binding, is destructive (= models.EffectClass).
judgement.why: The later notes explicitly refuse a function node after checking that the node belongs to the active version and before checking destructive effect class.
